newsitem.title: POLAND: Olawa gives up planned vote on new issue.
newsitem.headline: Olawa gives up planned vote on new issue.

text.p: The management of Polish non-ferrous metals smelter Olawa SA scrapped the vote on a new share issue from the agenda of the general shareholders' meeting in December or early next year, a senior Olawa official said on Thursday.

Olawa's deputy president Andrzej Latka told Reuters the management would only ask shareholders to consider ways of acquiring capital which the company needed to invest in companies supplying it with raw materials.

The management earlier planned to ask shareholders to approve a new issue of 1,350,000 shares to raise about 20 million zlotys to buy a 25 percent stake in Zaklady Gorniczo-Hutnicze Boleslaw and Huta Cynku Miasteczko Slaskie.

"The new share issue will not be voted on at the next shareholders' meeting, but we will ask our shareholders whether we should find funds we need through a share issue or other forms such as bank loans," Latka said.

He said the management had scrapped the new issue vote from the agenda because it feared that uncertainty over the timing and method of Boleslaw's future sale might make shareholders reluctant to approve a new issue to buy a stake in the company.

Olawa's main shareholders are the state treasury, holding a 16.7-percent stake, Polish mutual trust fund Pioneer 10.4 percent, Irena 10 percent, bank Pekao SA 7.7 percent and Bank Gdanski 5.0 percent.
